sections.title: The letter err
paragraphs: The letter is named (err) /ɛr/. It makes one sound. You hear it in the word (róka) /ˈroːkɒ/, which means fox. This letter always represents a rolled sound in Hungarian speech.

sections.title: Making the sound
paragraphs: Put the tip of your tongue on the ridge behind your upper teeth. Blow air over the tip so it vibrates quickly. This is a trill, a consonant where the tongue taps many times very fast. Turn your voice on so your throat vibrates. Put a hand on your throat to feel the buzz.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: This letter always makes the same sound in all positions. You roll your tongue tip behind your teeth every time. You can hear this sound clearly in the word (piros) /ˈpiroʃ/.

sections.title: Avoiding English habits
paragraphs: Do not pull your tongue back as in red. Do not curl your tongue tip backward into the mouth. Instead, keep the tip forward on the ridge behind your teeth. Make the tip tap rapidly against that ridge. Tap it lightly like the quick sound in water.
